subject: Pilot extension and performance backstop options for Trellis Analytics
messages:
From: Elsa Moore <elsa@brightarc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot cadence and next-step ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Trellis is excited about the accuracy improvements we saw on our data. Before we move to a conversion conversation, procurement asked whether we could either:

- add a short 2-week extension to the current timeboxed pilot (we've burned faster than expected), or
- top up the pilot with additional inference credits so we can complete a final integration sprint.

They also flagged a concern: if live latency or throughput dips during our stress test next week, would Redwood consider a performance "backstop" (small credit) to offset delays to our schedule?

Can you share an example pricing split for time extension vs credit top-up and any precedent for a performance backstop? Procurement wants a formal ask by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Elsa Moore
Head of Platform Integrations
Trellis Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elsa Moore <elsa@brightarc.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence and next-step ask

Hi Elsa — thanks, glad the demo landed. Quick answers and a proposed path: 

Options (high level):
1) Two-week time extension: $0 (we typically waive a modest fee for a 1–2 week runway for customers with active exec sponsorship) — we would add 14 days to the current pilot end date and keep the same rate card.
2) Credit top-up: we can issue a one-time block of inference credits (token-equivalent) — we suggest a 20% credit top-up relative to the pilot burn rate to cover the final sprint.

Performance backstop (proposal):
- If average 95th percentile latency exceeds the SLA in the stress runs, Redwood will issue a $2,500 service credit applied to the conversion invoice. This is modest but covers scheduling impact and shows operational confidence.

I've attached a pricing matrix that lays out examples and the math for each option (pricing_matrix.xlsx). 

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm preferred path (extension vs credits) and I’ll route a short SOW amendment to legal.
- If you want the backstop, we add a one-paragraph clause to the SOW.

Looping Priya on the ops/CS side for ramp details. David, can legal eyeball the proposed backstop language?

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elsa Moore <elsa@brightarc.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence and next-step ask

Thanks Ben — from CS/eng perspective:

- If Trellis picks the two-week extension we’ll allocate a 1-day onboarding window to re-run telemetry and a targeted set of checks; no charge.
- If they prefer credits, recommend a 20–25% top-up to avoid mid-sprint throttling.
- For the backstop, ops prefers a credit (applied to their invoice) rather than a service-level break clause — simpler to operationalize.

I'll draft a brief SOW paragraph that defines the stress-test window and the metrics that trigger the credit. Attaching sample language to my follow-up.

—Priya
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elsa Moore <elsa@brightarc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence and next-step ask

Ben/Priya — thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement prefers a 10-business-day extension plus a modest backstop credit tied to the scheduled stress test. Their reasoning: less paperwork for a short extension, but we want the backstop to cover any missed launch commitments.

Two questions before I route this internally: 
1) Can you convert the $2,500 backstop into credits (token-equivalent) so it’s applied directly to usage?
2) Can you push a short SOW amendment and a DocuSign link for signature?

If you can get me that today we’ll try to finalize by COB tomorrow.

Best,
Elsa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elsa Moore <elsa@brightarc.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence and next-step ask

Elsa — great, we can do that. Quick summary of the final terms we’ll put in the SOW amendment: 

- Pilot amendment: add 10 business days to the current end date.
- Credit backstop: convert the $2,500 backstop to a token credit equivalent (applied to the account if the 95th percentile latency during the agreed stress window is > SLA).
- Stress window & trigger: one 4-hour scheduled stress test during the extension; measurable trigger is 95th percentile latency above agreed threshold measured over the window.

Attached is the revised SOW draft (SOW_Trellis_v2.pdf) and the pricing matrix for transparency. I’ve also created the DocuSign envelope and shared link here: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/SharedLink/abc123-docusign — that will pre-fill the amendment. HubSpot deal has been updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/DL-2024-782

If that language looks good to you, sign the DocuSign and we’ll schedule the stress run with Priya’s team.

Thanks — Ben
